I can't identify a definite source, so this is a best guess. The most likely Austin is J.L. Austin, and critics may call him a "naive empiricist" because he treated everyday linguistic usage and perceptual appearances as plain data. On that reading he paid too little attention to the theoretical assumptions behind how that data is collected and interpreted. If you mean a different Austin, such as John Austin the legal theorist, or you can tell me where you saw the phrase, I can give a more precise answer.
